name: Ancient Grains
summary: Chewy ancient grains take the lead: barley risotto, quinoa tabbouleh with salmon, buckwheat with roast vegetables, farro with lemon chicken and millet porridge. Beans or fish in most meals, no bread, pasta or rice, and five dishes that cook once and make the next lunch.
howItWorks:
**Grains are the star.** Barley, quinoa, buckwheat, millet, farro and oats fill the plate at most meals, always with beans, fish, meat or eggs and plenty of vegetables. There is no bread, flour, pasta or rice. Farro stands in for freekeh in the chicken dish.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's barley risotto, Wednesday's buckwheat tray, Thursday's farro and chicken and Saturday's stuffed squash each make two portions, and Monday's quinoa salad feeds Wednesday's lunch too. Cool cooked grains within 1 hour in a shallow container, keep them up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot. Yogurt, parsley and the second egg go on cold.

**Fish and protein.** Salmon on Tuesday and trout on Friday are always cooked fresh, with tinned salmon and sardines as snacks for **omega-3 and vitamin D**. Eggs show up at three breakfasts, in Wednesday's buckwheat dish and in two snacks for **choline**, with chicken, turkey, beef, tuna and chickpeas covering the rest.

**What changes with size.** Light cuts oil, nuts and cheese so lunch and dinner keep a real scoop of grain, and swaps Tuesday's and Thursday's breakfasts for an egg and chickpea scramble and a berry yogurt bowl. Meat and fish get smaller, the chicken most, and six days lose a snack. Big grows the grains, meat, fish and beans and adds a snack every day.

recipes.name: Overnight oats with berries and almonds
recipes.about: Creamy rolled oats soaked in milk overnight with cinnamon, swirled with berries and topped with toasted almonds. The oats bring **slow, steady fibre**, and the almonds bring vitamin E and a little calcium.

ingredients.note: frozen, no need to thaw first

steps: Stir the oats, milk and cinnamon together in a jar or container with a lid, then fold in the frozen berries. Cover and chill overnight, or at least 6 hours.
In the morning, stir well. Eat it cold, or warm it in the microwave for 1 to 2 minutes until just steaming. Add a splash of milk if it has thickened.
Top with the almonds just before eating so they stay crunchy.
recipes.tip: Mix two jars at once and eat the second within 3 days. Keep soaked oats covered in the fridge, never on the counter. Frozen berries are fine for most people. If you are pregnant, over 65 or have a weakened immune system, heat them until steaming hot first or use fresh.

recipes.name: Cardamom millet porridge with apple and walnuts
recipes.about: Creamy, golden millet simmered in milk with cardamom and cinnamon, topped with warm apple slices and toasted walnuts. Millet is a **gluten-free grain** with magnesium and manganese, and the apple adds sweetness without any added sugar.
steps: Rinse the millet in a sieve under cold water. Toast it in a small dry pot over medium heat, stirring, until it smells nutty, about 2 minutes.

Add the milk, an equal amount of water, the cardamom and the cinnamon. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cook with the lid ajar, stirring often, until the millet is soft and the porridge is thick, about 15 minutes.
Add the diced apple for the last 4 minutes so it softens but keeps a little bite. Spoon into a bowl and top with the walnuts.
recipes.tip: For a quicker morning, simmer the millet in the water the night before, cool it within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep it covered in the fridge. In the morning, warm it with the milk and spices until steaming, about 5 minutes, then add the apple.

recipes.name: Savoury quinoa breakfast bowl with kale, tomato and a firm egg
recipes.about: Fluffy quinoa warmed with cumin, wilted kale and blistered tomatoes, topped with firm-cooked eggs and a squeeze of lemon, with a glass of milk on the side. The **eggs and quinoa** bring choline and complete protein, and the kale and tomato add calcium, iron and vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume with a pinch of salt, covered, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender, about 14 minutes. Rest it, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Meanwhile, wash the kale and tomatoes and halve the tomatoes. Warm half the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat and cook the tomatoes until they blister, about 3 minutes. Add the kale, cumin and a splash of water and stir until tender, about 3 minutes. Tip it onto the quinoa.
Wipe the pan, warm the rest of the oil and cook the eggs, turning once, until the whites are set and the yolks are completely firm, about 5 minutes.
Top the bowl with the eggs and the walnuts, finish with the lemon juice and serve with a glass of milk.
recipes.tip: When the bowl is on two mornings in a row, cook a double pot of quinoa on the first, cool the extra within 1 hour in a shallow container and keep it covered in the fridge. Warm it in the pan until steaming. Otherwise cook a fresh pot, which takes about 14 minutes.

recipes.name: Quinoa, tuna and chickpea salad with kale, tomato and dill
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Mediterranean tuna and chickpea salads, made with quinoa and kale
recipes.about: Fluffy quinoa tossed with light tuna, chickpeas, finely sliced kale, juicy tomatoes and a good handful of dill and parsley in a bright lemon dressing. The **tuna and chickpeas** make it properly filling, and the kale and tomato bring calcium and vitamin C to help absorb the iron.

ingredients.note: washed, stems removed, very finely sliced

steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume with a pinch of salt, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 14 minutes. Rest it, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Spread the quinoa in a shallow container to cool. Cool it within 1 hour, then chill it. Meanwhile, wash the kale, tomatoes, parsley and dill, then slice, halve and chop them.

Whisk the lemon juice and olive oil with a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss the kale with half the dressing and rub it with your fingers for a minute to soften it. Add the cooled quinoa, tuna, chickpeas, tomatoes, onion and herbs and toss with the rest.
Eat half now. Pack the second portion in a covered container in the fridge for Wednesday. Keep any opened tin of tuna covered in the fridge and use within 2 days.
recipes.tip: Eat the second portion within 3 days of cooking. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.

recipes.name: Smoky chickpea and tomato stew with barley and kale
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish and North African chickpea stews, with barley
recipes.about: A smoky stew of chickpeas, sweet cherry tomatoes and chewy barley, with kale stirred in and a spoonful of cool yogurt on top. The chickpeas and kale bring **fibre, folate and calcium**, and the barley keeps it hearty.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion with the garlic, smoked paprika and cumin, about 5 minutes.

Add the tomatoes and cook, pressing them with the back of a spoon, until they collapse, about 5 minutes. Add the barley and broth, then enough hot water to just cover. Simmer with the lid ajar, topping up with a splash of water if it gets dry, until the barley is tender, about 25 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and kale and simmer until the kale is tender, about 5 minutes. Add the lemon juice and a pinch of salt and pepper, and serve with the yogurt on top.
recipes.tip: Cool leftovers within 1 hour and use within 3 days, reheated until steaming. Add the yogurt cold.

recipes.name: Creamy barley and mushroom risotto with chicken and peas
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian mushroom risotto, made with pearled barley
recipes.about: Pearled barley simmered slowly in chicken broth until creamy like risotto, with golden mushrooms, seared chicken breast, sweet peas and spinach, finished with a little parmesan and lemon. The barley gives **soluble fibre and a creamy bite**, and the chicken and mushrooms bring B vitamins and protein.
steps: Wash the mushrooms, spinach and carrot. Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and season with a pinch of salt, pepper and the thyme.

Warm half the oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken until golden, about 4 minutes, then lift it out onto a plate. Wash your hands, the board and the knife after handling the raw chicken.
Add the rest of the oil, then the mushrooms, and cook until golden, about 5 minutes. Stir in the onion, garlic and carrot for 2 minutes, then the barley for 1 minute.
Add the broth, then hot water by the ladleful as it is absorbed, stirring now and then, until the barley is tender and creamy, about 22 minutes.
Return the chicken with the peas and cook until the peas are steaming hot and the chicken is cooked through, to 74 °C (165 °F). Fold in the spinach until wilted, then the parmesan and lemon juice.
Spoon half into a bowl. Cool the other portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill it for tomorrow. Reheat it once, until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F), with a splash of water.
recipes.tip: Pearled barley has had some of its bran polished off, which makes it creamy. For more chew, use hulled barley, the whole grain: soak it overnight and simmer about 25 minutes longer, adding hot water as needed. Keep the leftover risotto no more than 3 days.

recipes.name: Quinoa tabbouleh-style salad with roast salmon
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine tabbouleh, with quinoa in place of bulgur
recipes.about: A very green, lemony tabbouleh made with quinoa instead of bulgur, packed with parsley, cucumber and tomato, with chickpeas for body and a warm salmon fillet on top. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and all that parsley adds vitamin K and vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume with a pinch of salt, covered, until tender, about 14 minutes. Fluff it with a fork and spread it on a plate to cool for 10 minutes.

Pat the salmon dry, rub it with a little of the oil, the allspice and a pinch of salt and pepper, and roast on a lined tray until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily, about 12 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Wash the parsley, cucumber and tomatoes. Chop the parsley very finely, and dice the cucumber and onion.
Toss the quinoa with the parsley, vegetables, chickpeas, lemon juice and the rest of the oil. Taste for salt and lemon. Top with the salmon.
recipes.tip: Use salmon bought and cooked within a day, or thawed overnight in the fridge. If you cook extra quinoa, cool it within 1 hour and use it within 3 days.

recipes.name: Buckwheat with roasted vegetables, chickpeas, a firm egg and lemon yogurt
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European kasha and Middle Eastern roast vegetable trays
recipes.about: Nutty buckwheat under a tray of roasted carrots, broccoli, red pepper and red onion, with crisp spiced chickpeas, a firm-cooked egg and a cool lemon-garlic yogurt. **Buckwheat, chickpeas and egg** make a satisfying plate with lots of fibre, protein and choline, and the carrots and broccoli add vitamin A and C.

ingredients.note: boiled until the yolk is completely firm

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the vegetables. Toss the carrots, broccoli, pepper and onion on a tray with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Roast for 12 minutes.
Add the chickpeas to the tray, stir, and roast until the vegetables are browned at the edges and the chickpeas are crisp, about 15 minutes more.

Meanwhile, rinse the buckwheat, toast it in a dry pot for 1 minute, then add 2 parts water to 1 part buckwheat by volume and a pinch of salt. Simmer, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes. Rest it for 5 minutes, covered, then fluff.

Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water, peel one and halve it. Stir the yogurt with half the lemon juice, a very small grated clove of garlic and a pinch of salt.
Pile the buckwheat on a plate, top with the roast vegetables and chickpeas and the halved egg, then add the yogurt, the rest of the lemon and the parsley.

Cool the second portion of buckwheat and vegetables within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill. Keep the second egg in its shell, and the yogurt and parsley separate, and add them cold. Eat within 3 days.
recipes.tip: Tomorrow the second portion is great cold as a salad, or warm the grain and vegetables until steaming hot before adding the yogurt. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.

recipes.name: Farro with lemon-herb chicken, chickpeas and broccoli
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by freekeh dishes, made with farro
recipes.about: Chewy farro with seared lemon-garlic chicken, chickpeas, tender broccoli, juicy tomatoes and a big handful of parsley, lightly spiced with allspice and cinnamon and finished with toasted walnuts. It is **protein-rich and high in fibre**, and the herbs and lemon keep it fresh.
steps: Rinse the farro and simmer it in plenty of lightly salted water until tender but chewy, about 20 minutes. Drain well.
Meanwhile, toss the chicken with half the lemon juice, the garlic, allspice, cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken, turning, until golden and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 8 minutes. Lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli with a splash of water and cook, covered, until tender but still bright, about 5 minutes. Add the chickpeas and tomatoes for the last 2 minutes, until the chickpeas are hot.
Toss the farro with the broccoli, tomatoes, the rest of the lemon juice and the parsley. Top with the chicken and walnuts.
Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill it. Reheat it once for the next lunch until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F), adding the walnuts after.
recipes.tip: Farro is wheat, so it is not gluten-free. Freekeh, if you can find it, can go in its place. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.

recipes.name: Lemon-dill trout with barley, roasted beets and broccoli
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian fish with beets and dill, served on barley
recipes.about: Pan-roasted trout on lemony barley with sweet roasted beets and carrots, steamed broccoli and a cool dill-yogurt sauce. The trout brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the beets and broccoli add folate and fibre.

ingredients.note: washed, peeled and cut into small cubes
washed and cut into small cubes

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the beet and carrot cubes with half the oil and a pinch of salt and roast on a tray until tender at the edges, about 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the barley and simmer it in plenty of lightly salted water until tender, about 25 minutes. Drain well.
Stir the yogurt with the dill, half the lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of salt. Cover and chill.

Pat the trout dry and season with salt and pepper. Warm the rest of the oil in a heavy pan and cook the trout skin side down for 4 minutes, then turn and cook until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily, about 3 minutes more. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.

Steam the broccoli in a splash of water in a covered pot until tender but bright, about 5 minutes. Toss the barley with the broccoli, the roast beets and carrots and the rest of the lemon juice. Top with the trout and the dill-yogurt sauce.
recipes.tip: Use fresh trout bought and cooked within a day, or thawed overnight in the fridge. Leftover plain barley must be cooled within 1 hour and used within 3 days.

recipes.name: Stuffed butternut squash with turkey, quinoa, kale and apple
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North American harvest-style stuffed squash
recipes.about: Roasted butternut squash halves piled with sage-spiced turkey, quinoa, kale and diced apple, with toasted walnuts on top. The squash brings **vitamin A and potassium**, and the turkey and quinoa make it a full meal.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the squash, halve it lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Brush with a little of the oil and a pinch of salt and roast cut side down until a knife slides in easily, about 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume, covered, until tender, about 14 minutes. Fluff it. Wash the kale and chop it finely.

Warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan. Soften the onion with the garlic, sage and cinnamon, about 5 minutes. Add the turkey, break it up and cook until browned and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Stir in the kale, apple and broth until the kale wilts, then the quinoa. Season with salt and pepper.
Turn the squash cut side up, pile in the filling and return to the oven for 8 minutes. Top with the walnuts.
Cool the second portion within 1 hour, then chill it. Reheat it once for the next lunch until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: The filling also works in roasted peppers, or on its own as a quick quinoa and turkey hash.

recipes.name: Ginger beef and broccoli with toasty buckwheat
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese beef and broccoli, over buckwheat
recipes.about: Quick-seared beef strips with broccoli, carrot, kale and edamame in a ginger-garlic sauce, over toasty buckwheat. The beef and edamame bring **iron and protein**, and the broccoli and lemon add vitamin C, which helps your body absorb the iron from the edamame and greens.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat, toast it in a dry pot for 1 minute, then add 2 parts water to 1 part buckwheat by volume and a pinch of salt. Simmer, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes. Rest it for 5 minutes, covered, then fluff.
Meanwhile, mix the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of water. Toss the sliced beef with a third of it. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer until browned, about 2 minutes, and lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil, the broccoli, carrot and a splash of water, cover and steam for 4 minutes. Add the kale and edamame and stir until the kale wilts and the edamame is steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes.
Return the beef, pour in the rest of the sauce and toss until hot and cooked through, to 71 °C (160 °F), about 1 minute. Serve over the buckwheat.
recipes.tip: Slice the beef thinly while it is partly frozen, and cook it in a very hot pan so it sears instead of steaming.

recipes.name: Carrot and red pepper sticks with sumac yogurt dip
recipes.about: Crunchy sticks with a cool, garlicky yogurt dip dusted with tangy sumac. The carrot brings **vitamin A**, the pepper vitamin C and the yogurt calcium.
steps: Wash and cut the vegetables into sticks. Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice, a very small grated clove of garlic and a pinch of salt, then dust it with the sumac. Dip away.

recipes.name: Banana with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: A banana and a few walnuts with a shake of cinnamon. The banana brings **potassium**.
steps: Peel the banana, dust with the cinnamon and eat it with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Canned salmon in red pepper boats
recipes.about: Canned salmon with the bones, piled into red pepper halves with lemon. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats, vitamin D, B12 and calcium**.
steps: Wash the pepper, halve it lengthwise and remove the seeds. Flake the salmon into the pepper halves and squeeze over the lemon. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use within 2 days.

recipes.name: Apple with almonds and cinnamon
recipes.about: A crisp apple and a small handful of almonds with a shake of cinnamon. The apple brings **fibre** and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it, dust with the cinnamon and eat it with the almonds.

recipes.name: Orange with almonds
recipes.about: A juicy orange and a small handful of almonds. The orange brings **vitamin C** and the almonds bring vitamin E.
steps: Wash the orange, peel it and eat it with the almonds.

recipes.name: Crunchy cumin chickpeas
recipes.about: Oven-crisped chickpeas with cumin and smoked paprika. They bring **fibre, folate and plant protein**.

ingredients.note: drained, rinsed and patted very dry

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the very dry chickpeas with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt.
Roast on a tray, shaking once, until crisp, about 20 minutes. Cool for 5 minutes, then eat.

recipes.name: Apple with walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.about: A crisp apple and walnut halves with a shake of cinnamon. The apple brings **fibre**.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it, dust with the cinnamon and eat it with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Warm edamame with ginger and lemon
recipes.about: A bowl of warm edamame with lemon and a little fresh ginger. Edamame brings **protein, folate and fibre**.
steps: Cover the frozen edamame with boiling water for 3 minutes until steaming hot all the way through, then drain. Toss with the lemon juice, ginger and a pinch of salt.

recipes.name: Yogurt with berries and walnuts
recipes.about: Thick yogurt with berries and a few walnuts. It brings **calcium, protein and plant omega-3 fats**.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, stir in the berries and top with the walnuts. Frozen berries are fine for most people. If you are pregnant, over 65 or have a weakened immune system, heat them until steaming hot first, let them cool, or use fresh.

recipes.name: Sardines on tomato with lemon
recipes.about: Canned sardines piled on juicy tomatoes with lemon. The sardines bring **omega-3 fats, calcium and vitamin D**.
steps: Wash the tomatoes and slice them onto a plate. Lay the sardines over the tomatoes and squeeze over the lemon. Keep any opened tin covered in the fridge and use within 2 days.

recipes.name: Firm-boiled egg with cucumber, tomato and dill
recipes.about: A firm-boiled egg with crunchy cucumber, sweet cherry tomatoes and a scatter of fresh dill. The egg brings **choline and protein**.

ingredients.note: boiled until the yolk is completely firm

steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely firm. Cool in cold water, peel and halve. Serve with the washed tomatoes and cucumber, the dill and a pinch of pepper.

recipes.name: Orange segments with yogurt and walnuts
recipes.about: Orange segments with creamy yogurt and chopped walnuts. The orange brings **vitamin C**, the yogurt calcium and the walnuts plant omega-3 fats.
steps: Wash and peel the orange and separate the segments. Spoon the yogurt over and top with the walnuts.

recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Levantine tabbouleh, with quinoa in place of bulgur
recipes.about: A very green, lemony tabbouleh made with quinoa instead of bulgur, packed with parsley, cucumber and tomato, with chickpeas for body and a warm salmon fillet on top. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and all that parsley adds vitamin K and vitamin C.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume with a pinch of salt, covered, until tender, about 14 minutes. Fluff it with a fork and spread it on a plate to cool for 10 minutes.

Pat the salmon dry, rub it with a little of the oil, the allspice and a pinch of salt and pepper, and roast on a lined tray until the thickest part reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily, about 12 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.
Wash the parsley, cucumber and tomatoes. Chop the parsley very finely, and dice the cucumber and onion.
Toss the quinoa with the parsley, vegetables, chickpeas, lemon juice and the rest of the oil. Taste for salt and lemon. Top with the salmon.
recipes.tip: Use salmon bought and cooked within a day, or thawed overnight in the fridge. If you cook extra quinoa, cool it within 1 hour and use it within 3 days.

recipes.name: Buckwheat with roasted vegetables, chickpeas, a firm egg and lemon yogurt
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European kasha and Middle Eastern roast vegetable trays
recipes.about: Nutty buckwheat under a tray of roasted carrots, broccoli, red pepper and red onion, with crisp spiced chickpeas, a firm-cooked egg and a cool lemon-garlic yogurt. **Buckwheat, chickpeas and egg** make a satisfying plate with lots of fibre, protein and choline, and the carrots and broccoli add vitamin A and C.

ingredients.note: boiled until the yolk is completely firm

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Wash the vegetables. Toss the carrots, broccoli, pepper and onion on a tray with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Roast for 12 minutes.
Add the chickpeas to the tray, stir, and roast until the vegetables are browned at the edges and the chickpeas are crisp, about 15 minutes more.

Meanwhile, rinse the buckwheat, toast it in a dry pot for 1 minute, then add 2 parts water to 1 part buckwheat by volume and a pinch of salt. Simmer, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes. Rest it for 5 minutes, covered, then fluff.

Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolks are completely firm. Cool in cold water, peel one and halve it. Stir the yogurt with half the lemon juice, a very small grated clove of garlic and a pinch of salt.
Pile the buckwheat on a plate, top with the roast vegetables and chickpeas and the halved egg, then add the yogurt, the rest of the lemon and the parsley.

Cool the second portion of buckwheat and vegetables within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill. Keep the second egg in its shell, and the yogurt and parsley separate, and add them cold. Eat within 3 days.
recipes.tip: Tomorrow the second portion is great cold as a salad, or warm the grain and vegetables until steaming hot before adding the yogurt. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.

recipes.name: Farro with lemon-herb chicken, chickpeas and broccoli
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by freekeh dishes, made with farro
recipes.about: Chewy farro with seared lemon-garlic chicken, chickpeas, tender broccoli, juicy tomatoes and a big handful of parsley, lightly spiced with allspice and cinnamon and finished with toasted walnuts. It is **protein-rich and high in fibre**, and the herbs and lemon keep it fresh.
steps: Rinse the farro and simmer it in plenty of lightly salted water until tender but chewy, about 20 minutes. Drain well.
Meanwhile, toss the chicken with half the lemon juice, the garlic, allspice, cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw chicken.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken, turning, until golden and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 8 minutes. Lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli with a splash of water and cook, covered, until tender but still bright, about 5 minutes. Add the chickpeas and tomatoes for the last 2 minutes, until the chickpeas are hot.
Toss the farro with the broccoli, tomatoes, the rest of the lemon juice and the parsley. Top with the chicken and walnuts.
Cool the second portion within 1 hour in a shallow container, then chill it. Reheat it once for the next lunch until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F), adding the walnuts after.
recipes.tip: Farro is wheat, so it is not gluten-free. Freekeh, if you can find it, can go in its place. If you carry it to work, use a cold bag with an ice pack.

recipes.name: Lemon-dill trout with barley, roasted beets and broccoli
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Scandinavian fish with beets and dill, served on barley
recipes.about: Pan-roasted trout on lemony barley with sweet roasted beets and carrots, steamed broccoli and a cool dill-yogurt sauce. The trout brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the beets and broccoli add folate and fibre.

ingredients.note: washed, peeled and cut into small cubes
washed and cut into small cubes

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the beet and carrot cubes with half the oil and a pinch of salt and roast on a tray until tender at the edges, about 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the barley and simmer it in plenty of lightly salted water until tender, about 25 minutes. Drain well.
Stir the yogurt with the dill, half the lemon juice, the garlic and a pinch of salt. Cover and chill.

Pat the trout dry and season with salt and pepper. Warm the rest of the oil in a heavy pan and cook the trout skin side down for 4 minutes, then turn and cook until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F) and flakes easily, about 3 minutes more. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw fish.

Steam the broccoli in a splash of water in a covered pot until tender but bright, about 5 minutes. Toss the barley with the broccoli, the roast beets and carrots and the rest of the lemon juice. Top with the trout and the dill-yogurt sauce.
recipes.tip: Use fresh trout bought and cooked within a day, or thawed overnight in the fridge. Leftover plain barley must be cooled within 1 hour and used within 3 days.

recipes.name: Stuffed butternut squash with turkey, quinoa, kale and apple
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North American harvest-style stuffed squash
recipes.about: Roasted butternut squash halves piled with sage-spiced turkey, quinoa, kale and diced apple, with toasted walnuts on top. The squash brings **vitamin A and potassium**, and the turkey and quinoa make it a full meal.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Wash the squash, halve it lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Brush with a little of the oil and a pinch of salt and roast cut side down until a knife slides in easily, about 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa and simmer it in 2 parts water to 1 part quinoa by volume, covered, until tender, about 14 minutes. Fluff it. Wash the kale and chop it finely.

Warm the rest of the oil in a wide pan. Soften the onion with the garlic, sage and cinnamon, about 5 minutes. Add the turkey, break it up and cook until browned and cooked through to 74 °C (165 °F), about 6 minutes. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw turkey.
Stir in the kale, apple and broth until the kale wilts, then the quinoa. Season with salt and pepper.
Turn the squash cut side up, pile in the filling and return to the oven for 8 minutes. Top with the walnuts.
Cool the second portion within 1 hour, then chill it. Reheat it once for the next lunch until steaming hot to 74 °C (165 °F).
recipes.tip: The filling also works in roasted peppers, or on its own as a quick quinoa and turkey hash.

recipes.name: Ginger beef and broccoli with toasty buckwheat
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Chinese beef and broccoli, over buckwheat
recipes.about: Quick-seared beef strips with broccoli, carrot, kale and edamame in a ginger-garlic sauce, over toasty buckwheat. The beef and edamame bring **iron and protein**, and the broccoli and lemon add vitamin C, which helps your body absorb the iron from the edamame and greens.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat, toast it in a dry pot for 1 minute, then add 2 parts water to 1 part buckwheat by volume and a pinch of salt. Simmer, covered, until the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes. Rest it for 5 minutes, covered, then fluff.
Meanwhile, mix the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of water. Toss the sliced beef with a third of it. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Sear the beef in a single layer until browned, about 2 minutes, and lift it out.

Add the rest of the oil, the broccoli, carrot and a splash of water, cover and steam for 4 minutes. Add the kale and edamame and stir until the kale wilts and the edamame is steaming hot all the way through, about 3 minutes.
Return the beef, pour in the rest of the sauce and toss until hot and cooked through, to 71 °C (160 °F), about 1 minute. Serve over the buckwheat.
recipes.tip: Slice the beef thinly while it is partly frozen, and cook it in a very hot pan so it sears instead of steaming.

recipes.name: Firm egg scramble with chickpeas, kale and tomato
recipes.about: A quick pan of firm-cooked eggs with chickpeas, wilted kale and blistered tomatoes, with a glass of milk on the side. The **eggs and chickpeas** bring choline and protein, and the kale adds calcium and vitamin K.
steps: Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat and cook the tomatoes until they blister, about 3 minutes. Add the kale, cumin and a splash of water and stir until tender, about 3 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and stir until hot, about 2 minutes. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour them in and stir until completely set and firm, about 3 minutes.
Spoon into a bowl and serve with a glass of milk.
recipes.tip: Make it your own with baby spinach in place of the kale, or a pinch of chili flakes with the cumin.

recipes.name: Berry yogurt bowl with apple and almonds
recipes.about: Thick yogurt with berries, diced apple, almonds and cinnamon. It brings **calcium, protein and vitamin E** with fruit for fibre.
steps: Wash and dice the apple.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and stir in the berries and apple.
Top with the almonds and a dusting of cinnamon, and eat straight away while the almonds are crunchy.
recipes.tip: Frozen berries are fine for most people. If you are pregnant, over 65 or have a weakened immune system, heat them until steaming hot first, let them cool, or use fresh.
